chunks: From him, from Ahmad, from Musa ibn al-Qasim and Abu Qatadah, all of them, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both), who said:

I asked him about the man who prostrates on pebbles and cannot press his forehead fully to the ground. He said: 'He should move his forehead until he can press it, thereby moving the pebbles away from his forehead, and he should not raise his head.'
ai.seo_question: How should one perform prostration if pebbles prevent the forehead from touching the ground directly?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the fiqh of *sujud* on uneven surfaces, emphasizing that the essential requirement is the forehead's contact with the earth rather than a perfectly flat plane. The ruling instructs the worshipper to shift the forehead laterally to clear pebbles without lifting the head, preserving the continuity of the prostration posture. This reflects the Shia scholarly principle of facilitating worship (*taysir*) while maintaining the strict physical conditions (*shurut*) of the prayer.
